summary: x402 natively binds the payee and amount in the client's authorization, bounds most authorizations in time, prevents replay and returns a transaction hash. It leaves identity, consent, budgets, disputes and reputation to SDKs, facilitators or other protocols. A signed exact payment has no recall message; the signer can only cancel an unused EVM authorization on chain, outside x402. The best places for an independent controls layer are the client before signing (policy hooks, payTo allowlists, budgets) and the facilitator at settlement (screening).

native.note: Identity is optional and separate from payment: sign-in-with-x (CAIP-122 wallet proof), auth-hints (OAuth 2.0 with DPoP) and RFC 9421 agent signatures in cloudflare:402.
No registry in x402. ERC-8004 can record that an agent accepts x402; cloudflare:402 needs the signature agent registered with Cloudflare.
The protocol has no consent object. The browser paywall asks a human in the UI; agents rely on mandates from other protocols such as AP2.
Budgets are out of scope in the spec. The TypeScript client applies spendControls by default (default assets only, $1 per payment); upto signs a ceiling.
With EIP-3009 and Permit2 the client's signature covers payTo and the amount; with ERC-7710 the delegation's caveats must. EVM upto also names the one facilitator allowed to settle.

validAfter, validBefore, the Permit2 deadline, maxTimeoutSeconds and Lightning invoice expiry bound exact, upto, auth-capture and Lightning authorizations. Batch-settlement vouchers carry no expiry and stay claimable until the escrow is drained; ERC-7710 delegations carry whatever limits the delegator set.

x402 has no revocation message. The signer can race the facilitator by canceling an unused EVM authorization on chain before settlement: EIP-3009 cancelAuthorization (Base USDC implements it), Permit2 nonce invalidation or revoking an ERC-7710 delegation. auth-capture adds void and client reclaim after the capture deadline; batch-settlement channels allow timed withdrawal.

The core specification defines no step-up to the human. The auth-hints extension lets a server require OAuth authentication for specific payment options (a 401 challenge), which identifies the client but is not a risk-based escalation.
Single-use 32-byte nonces enforced by EIP-3009 tokens, Permit2 nonces, cumulative vouchers, and replay stores for Lightning payment hashes.
PAYMENT-RESPONSE carries the transaction hash; the optional offer-receipt extension signs offers and receipts (TypeScript only).

No dispute or chargeback process. exact defines no refund; auth-capture adds void, refund and reclaim, batch-settlement channels refund unclaimed escrow, Solana upto returns unused escrow, and third parties such as x402r add arbitration.
None in x402. ERC-8004 feedback can carry proofOfPayment for an x402 payment.

On-chain settlements (EVM, Solana) are public but look like ordinary transfers; /supported, Bazaar and x402scan expose endpoints and 402 offers. Payment payloads, Lightning payments and cloudflare:402 commitments are not public.
No protocol kill switch. Clients stop by policy or spendControls; servers stop by removing routes; facilitators can refuse to settle.

gaps.title: No protocol budget
gaps.description: Client-side budget management is out of scope. Caps exist only in SDKs and wallets, and can be switched off with spendControls false.

gaps.title: No recall message for a signed exact payment
gaps.description: Once a client signs, the authorization stays valid until validBefore unless the client cancels it on chain first (EIP-3009 cancelAuthorization or Permit2 nonce invalidation, outside x402), racing the facilitator. The exact scheme itself has no recall step.

gaps.title: No disputes
gaps.description: exact defines no refund, and upto only returns unused or undelivered escrow on Solana; neither has a refund after settlement, and the protocol has no dispute process.

gaps.title: No identity or consent object
gaps.description: The payment says nothing about who the client is beyond its paying address, or about what a user approved; optional extensions and other protocols fill this.

gaps.title: Weak on-chain labeling
gaps.description: An exact EIP-3009 payment is an ordinary token transfer on chain, so monitors cannot easily isolate x402 traffic without builder codes or facilitator data.

controlPoints.what: Decide whether to pay at all: allowlists, budgets, asset and network policy.
controlPoints.how: Client policies and hooks (onPaymentRequired, onBeforePaymentCreation) and spendControls in the SDK.

controlPoints.what: Limit what a signature can do.
controlPoints.how: Short validBefore windows, low upto ceilings, wallet-level signing policies and key isolation.

controlPoints.what: Check requests before they reach the seller.
controlPoints.how: Payment middleware, CDN gateways such as Cloudflare's, and RFC 9421 agent identity in cloudflare:402.

controlPoints.what: Screen and deduplicate before money moves.
controlPoints.how: Facilitator KYT and OFAC screening, onBeforeSettle hooks, atomic deduplication across settle workers.
auth-capture refunds, third-party x402r, transaction-hash receipts, contract events and x402scan monitoring.

checklist.item: Pin the expected payTo per seller and refuse anything else before signing.
checklist.why: The signature protects payTo only after you sign it.

checklist.item: Keep spendControls on and set a cap lower than the $1 default for unattended agents.
checklist.why: Budgets are not part of the protocol.

checklist.item: Verify against your own requirements for the requested route, not the accepted object the client echoed.
Treat a settle timeout as unknown and reconcile on chain before retrying.
checklist.why: The facilitator may already have settled.

checklist.item: Keep @x402 packages current and test encoded-path variants of paid routes.
checklist.why: Several releases fixed payment bypasses in route matching.

checklist.item: Store every PAYMENT-RESPONSE transaction hash with the request it paid for.
checklist.why: It is the only receipt exact provides.

checklist.item: Strip personal data from resource URLs and descriptions.
Use auth-capture when buyers need refunds or delivery is delayed.
